title: Air-gapped bootstrap validation + Terraform interfaces (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft of a repeatable, minimal bootstrap + validation playbook for air-gapped installs. Goal is a small, testable checklist and a clear Terraform module surface that teams can wire into their environment to produce:
  - an offline artifact bundle (images, charts, binaries, kustomize overlays)
  - an offline OCI registry layout or image archive consumable by containerd/ctr
  - a post-import validation harness that asserts cluster/operator health before handing control to higher-level installers

Scope and non-goals:
  - Focus: initial install + first upgrade (0 -> 1 and 1 -> 2). Not covering long-term sync cadence or delta-only syncs.
  - Non-goal: automated vendor signing chain (we include checksum validation and optional vendor cert support but not a full PKI design here).

Assumptions (project/infra):
  - Customer provides an isolated airgap transfer host (sized ~8 vCPUs, 32GB, ephemeral storage 1TB) with HTTPS egress to a staging mirror (internal) OR removable media ingestion capability.
  - Target Kubernetes clusters use containerd or CRI-compatible runtime and have image import APIs available (ctr images import or crictl load).
  - We can stage files on customer network under a known path (e.g. /opt/redwood/airgap/bundles/<release>).

High-level flow (happy path):
  1) TF module (mirror-builder) runs in online environment to download and stage artifacts into a bundle directory. Produces bundle.tar.gz + checksums.json + manifest.yaml.
  2) Transfer operator takes bundle.tar.gz into the air-gapped environment (SCP, external disk).
  3) On air-gapped side run 'bundle-bootstrap' that: expands archive, imports images into local registry or directly into nodes, loads charts and manifests into cluster, applies CRDs, and runs post-import validations.
  4) If validation passes, mark release as available in local registry and signal install/ops to proceed with normal onboarding. If not, capture logs and produce failure artifacts for debugging.

Terraform module interface (proposal, minimal):
  Module name: redwood/airgap/mirror-builder (draft)
  - Inputs (variables - minimal types shown):
      mirror_source_urls: list(string)  # primary endpoints/feeds to mirror (models, charts, images)
      release_tag: string               # e.g. v2024-05-01
      output_dir: string                # local path where bundle is written
      include_helm_charts: bool         # default true
      image_selection_file: string     # relative path to a YAML that lists images/repos/tags to mirror
      retry_policy: map(string)        # e.g. {max_attempts=3, backoff_seconds=10}
      vendor_certs_path: string        # optional path to CA bundle to trust
  - Outputs:
      bundle_path: string              # absolute path to bundle.tar.gz
      manifest_sha256: string
      staging_artifact_count: number   # rough count useful for validation
  - Notes on implementation: favour using external 'local-exec' helpers for s3/registry access where provider SDKs are unreliable in the customer environment. Keep the TF module orchestrating scripts rather than embedding heavy logic in HCL.

Bundle layout (recommended):
  bundle-<release>/
    README.md                  # summary produced at build time
    manifest.yaml              # lists images, charts, binaries, versions, checksums
    checksums.json             # sha256 sums for each file
    images/                    # optional OCI tarballs or oci-layout directory
      images-repo1.tar         # docker save style OR ORAS/oci-layout dir
    registry-layout/           # optional: filesystem layout for local registry push (skopeo/registry copy artifacts)
    helm/                      # tarballs of charts + index
    manifests/                 # kustomize/overlays used for install
    binaries/                  # small tools (kubectl, cert-tools) pinned versions

Tooling notes and example commands (for builder scripts):
  - Copy images into oci/archive: docker pull && docker save OR skopeo copy docker://repo:tag oci:/out/images-repo1 --dest-tls-verify=false
  - Produce tar with predictable order for stable checksums: tar --sort=name --mtime='UTC 2024-01-01' -cf bundle.tar images/ registry-layout/ helm/ manifests/ binaries/ README.md
  - Compute checksums: sha256sum bundle.tar > bundle.tar.sha256 && jq -n --arg sha "$(sha256sum bundle.tar | awk '{print $1}')" '{bundle: $sha}' > checksums.json
  - Import into containerd on node: ctr -n=k8s.io images import /opt/redwood/airgap/bundles/<release>/images-repo1.tar
  - Push into a local registry: skopeo copy oci:/tmp/images-repo1 docker://registry.local:5000/repo --dest-cert-dir=/opt/registry/certs

Post-import validation checklist (to run on air-gapped side, automated where possible):
  Pre-flight on transfer host:
    - [ ] Verify bundle.tar.gz sha256 matches checksums.json and manifest.yaml version.
    - [ ] Ensure target path permissions are writable by installer user.
    - [ ] Confirm presence of required binaries (kubectl, ctr/crictl).
  Image & registry validation:
    - [ ] Import or push images listed in manifest. Record import duration and any failures.
    - [ ] For registry mode: verify HTTP(s) responses from registry endpoint and validate cert chains if provided.
    - [ ] Attempt pod creation for a tiny smoke image from the registry (busybox) and run 'echo hello' to confirm pull succeeds.
  Kubernetes resource validation:
    - [ ] Apply CRDs only (dry run first if possible).
    - [ ] Apply control-plane operator manifests and wait for pods to hit Ready state within the timeout window.
    - [ ] Validate operator logs for immediate errors (imagePullBackOff, crashloop, cert errors).
  Functional checks (lightweight):
    - [ ] Run a 10 request text generation smoke test against the deployed API (if part of the bundle).
    - [ ] Run a small embedding/health endpoint against a non-sensitive sample input.
  Observability & artifact capture on failure:
    - [ ] Collect container logs (kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=operator --tail=500).
    - [ ] Collect images manifest (ctr -n=k8s.io images ls --digests).
    - [ ] Save /var/log/syslog or journalctl entries around the time of failure.

Upgrade plan (0 -> 1 and 1 -> 2 pattern):
  Concepts:
    - 'install' = initial import + operator install + basic smoke tests.
    - 'minor-upgrade' = changes that don't touch DB schema or K8s CR semantics.
    - 'major-upgrade' = requires migration, roll-forward hooks, or CRD conversions.
  Steps for a controlled upgrade in an airgapped environment (example minor upgrade):
    1) Build a delta bundle containing new images + updated charts. Produce manifest-delta.yaml.
    2) Run pre-upgrade validations on running cluster (health, CR status, PV health).
    3) Import images into registry or nodes, tag with new release.
    4) Apply charts with canary set to 1 replica for operator/controller first. Wait for stability window (15-30m).
    5) If stable, scale up to desired replicas. Run smoke test.
    6) Capture metrics and compare to baseline. If any regression, trigger rollback plan.

Rollback plan (simple):
  - Keep previous bundle (bundle-<release>-previous) present in /opt/redwood/airgap/bundles.
  - If operator cannot rollback automatically, replace images in registry to point to previous digest and redeploy controllers with previous chart.
  - For more complex migrations, maintain migration scripts that are reversible where possible; include 'down' steps in the bundle under migrations/down/

Observability + debug artifacts produced by the bootstrap script (recommended):
  - /opt/redwood/airgap/artifacts/<release>/validation-report.json (structured but small)
  - logs/installer.log (rotated)
  - captured-pod-logs.tar.gz
  - registry-health.json
  - ctr-images-ls.txt

Known issues & open questions (working list):
  - How much of the mirroring should be 'smart' (only changed images) vs brute-force full mirror? Tradeoffs: speed vs correctness for first-time vs repeat sync.
  - Handling private base images (customer base OS images requiring credentials). We need an agreed pattern for credential injection into the mirror builder.
  - Large model files (multi-GB) cause bundle growth and slow transfers: consider splitting model artifacts into a separate transfer channel with resumable transfer tool (rsync over SSH with checksums or aria2c).
  - Windows-based airgap hosts (customer-provided) vary widely; focus initially on Linux-based transfer hosts.

Next steps / TODOs:
  - [ ] Convert TF interface into a lightweight module skeleton (HCL + helper scripts). Owner: Diego. ETA: 2024-06-01.
  - [ ] Wire a CI job that builds a sample bundle for the 'canary' release and runs the local validation harness on a lightweight k3s lab. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2024-06-15.
  - [ ] Validate import speed/throughput numbers on representative networks (10GB external drive vs 1GbE scp). Add recommendations to README. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2024-06-30.

Notes to reviewers:
  - This is intentionally pragmatic: TF should act as orchestration and reproducible artifact producer, not as a data-pump. Heavy lifting implemented in shell/python helpers.
  - I'm flagging the 'checksums.json' pattern as central: if we standardize JSON schema for manifests, downstream validation tooling becomes much easier.

If you're editing this doc: keep changes short and add your initials to the top change list. Comments inline are fine.

Change-log (brief):
  - 2024-05-10: initial draft (Aisha)
  - 2024-06-02: added TF interface proposal (Diego)
  - 2024-07-12: added detailed validation checklist and CLI examples (Maya)
  - 2024-08-02: minor edits + open questions added (Samir)
